Sustaining the Unsustainable? Greek Government Debt Before and After the Euro
Job market paper · Working paper · [Month Year] · PDF


Abstract

Using hand-collected fiscal data for 1957–2008, I ask how Greece sustained a high and apparently unsustainable level of government debt for decades, even though conventional empirical sustainability criteria point to unsustainability since at least the 1970s. I argue that the institutional transition into the euro area explains the timing. Before the euro, inflation, monetary accommodation, and currency depreciation relaxed the effective financing constraint and postponed the crisis. Euro membership removed these mechanisms.
